links.comparator_used: Pre-AI period (Sept 2021 to Aug 2022) without the AI-guided bundle, compared with the post-AI period (2023) after a 4-month rollout; pre-post quasi-experimental design with matching adjustment
links.effect: CDI incidence 5.76 vs 5.65 per 10 000 patient-days, absolute difference -0.11 (95% CI -1.43 to 1.18; P = .85). Piperacillin-tazobactam -9.64 days of therapy per 1000 days present (95% CI -12.93 to -6.28; P < .001), clindamycin -1.04 (95% CI -1.60 to -0.47; P = .03), ampicillin-sulbactam -2.82 (P = .03). Piperacillin-tazobactam relative reduction 16.8% (95% CI 8.0%-24.6%) in AI-alerted high-risk patients, with no significant change in low-risk patients.
links.tradeoff: Poor adherence to the enhanced hand hygiene component. Of 17 practitioners interviewed, 6 ignored the BPAs and 10 could not recall their content, with signs of alert fatigue. Pharmacists engaged consistently with the alerts. Residual confounding and concurrent stewardship initiatives cannot be excluded.
links.quote: In this quality improvement study, although the implementation of an AI-guided infection prevention bundle for CDI was not associated with a significant reduction in CDI incidence, it was associated with reductions in the use of CDI-associated antimicrobials, demonstrating the potential of AI-guided antimicrobial stewardship.

design_hint: AI risk-alert-guided infection prevention bundle (hand hygiene, antimicrobial stewardship) with pre/post comparison
